C# Parameter object

Naming rules

suffix Purpose Example

*Ref

refers to an existing object and is only responsible for locating resources.

NodeRef、PortRef、BindingRef

*Params

Complete parameters for an interface call

CreateNodeParams、RuntimeRunParams

*Update

Modify existing configuration, parameters or runtime data

NodeParamUpdate、RuntimeParamsUpdate

It can be understood as follows: * Ref is "Who do I want to operate?" * Params is "I’m going to do a complete thing" * Update is "I want to change something that already exists into something"

Basic writing method

C# Parameter objects are all under the AtomSdk.Models namespace:

using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Models;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

var node = await client.Node.CreateNodeInfoAsync(new CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "ResizeImage"));
Console.WriteLine($"Create node request status: {node.Status}");
var activated = await client.Node.ActivateNodeResultAsync(new NodeRef("my_graph", node.NodeId));
Console.WriteLine($"activation request status: {activated.Status}");
await client.Runtime.GetBindedOutputValueAsync(new BindingRef("my_graph", "result"));

For objects with many fields, it is recommended to use named parameters to avoid writing the input and output terminals in reverse:

await client.Node.ConnectNodesInfoAsync(
    new NodeConnectionParams(
        "my_graph",
        outputNodeId: resizeNodeId,
        outputPortName: "resized_image",
        inputNodeId: detectNodeId,
        inputPortName: "image"));

Common parameter objects

Graph

Parameter object is used for Constructor

CreateGraphParams

Graph.CreateGraphAsync

new CreateGraphParams(graphName, description?)

CopyGraphParams

Graph.CopyGraphAsync

new CopyGraphParams(graphName, newGraphName)

EditGraphNameParams

Graph.EditGraphNameAsync

new EditGraphNameParams(graphName, newGraphName)

EditGraphCommentParams

Graph.EditGraphCommentAsync

new EditGraphCommentParams(graphName, comment)

LoadGraphParams

Graph.LoadGraphAsync

new LoadGraphParams(graphName, filePath)

ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams

Graph.ImportExtensionNodesByPathAsync

new ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams(extensionNodes)

ExportGraphParams

Graph.ExportGraphAsync

new ExportGraphParams(graphName, dlModelsInfo?, customNodes?)

 
var graph = await client.Graph.CreateGraphInfoAsync(
    new CreateGraphParams("demo_graph", "created by C# SDK"));
Console.WriteLine($"Create graph request status: {graph.Status}");

await client.Graph.CopyGraphAsync(
    new CopyGraphParams("demo_graph", "demo_graph_backup"));
await client.Graph.EditGraphNameAsync(new EditGraphNameParams("demo_graph", "demo_graph_v2"));
await client.Graph.EditGraphCommentAsync(new EditGraphCommentParams("demo_graph_v2", "New process notes"));

Node

Parameter object is used for

NodeRef

Delete, query, activate, initialize, update existing nodes

CreateNodeParams

Create node

CreateDynamicNodeParams

Create dynamic IO node

CopyNodeParams

Copy node

ChangeNodeIOParams

Modify dynamic node input and output

CreateGraphNodeParams

Created from existing subgraphs graph node

GenerateGraphNodeByNodesParams

is packaged and generated by multiple nodes graph node

NodeConnectionParams

Connect or disconnect nodes

PortRef

Read node port data or point cloud

NodeParamUpdate

Set node parameters

NodeBindingUpdate

Set node binding name

EditNodeCommentParams

Modify node remarks

 
var node = await client.Node.CreateNodeInfoAsync(
    new CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "DetectAndSegment", "Detect node"));
Console.WriteLine($"Create node request status: {node.Status}");

await client.Node.ActivateNodeResultAsync(
    new NodeRef("my_graph", node.NodeId));
await client.Node.CreateGraphNodeAsync(new CreateGraphNodeParams("my_graph", "SubFlow", "sub_graph_alpha"));
await client.Node.GenerateGraphNodeByNodesAsync(
    new GenerateGraphNodeByNodesParams("my_graph", "PackedNode", new[] { "node-a", "node-b" }));
await client.Node.EditNodeCommentAsync(new EditNodeCommentParams("my_graph", node.NodeId, "This is a new note"));

The dynamic IO node needs to pass the IO configuration agreed by the server:

await client.Node.CreateDynamicIoNodeAsync(
    new CreateDynamicNodeParams(
        "my_graph",
        "DynamicNode",
        new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["inputs"] = new[] { new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["name"] = "image_in" } } }));
await client.Node.ChangeNodeIoAsync(
    new ChangeNodeIOParams(
        "my_graph",
        node.NodeId,
        new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["outputs"] = new[] { new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["name"] = "mask_out" } } }));

When connecting nodes, the field order is "output first, input last":

await client.Node.ConnectNodesInfoAsync(
    new NodeConnectionParams(
        "my_graph",
        outputNodeId: resizeNodeId,
        outputPortName: "resized_image",
        inputNodeId: detectNodeId,
        inputPortName: "image"));

When setting ordinary parameters, value can be string, numerical value, bool and other basic types:

await client.Node.SetNodeParamDataInfoAsync(
    new NodeParamUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        nodeId,
        "threshold",
        "run_params",
        0.7));

When setting file parameters, it is recommended to pass FileInfo, SDK will be uploaded by file:

await client.Node.SetNodeParamDataInfoAsync(
    new NodeParamUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        nodeId,
        "model",
        "init_params",
        new FileInfo("/models/detector.onnx")));

If the file content already exists, you can also pass byte[]:

byte[] modelBytes = await File.ReadAllBytesAsync("/models/detector.onnx");
await client.Node.SetNodeParamDataAsync(
    new NodeParamUpdate("my_graph", nodeId, "model", "init_params", modelBytes));

Binding names are typically "inputs", "outputs", "init_params", or "run_params":

await client.Node.SetBindingNameInfoAsync(
    new NodeBindingUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        nodeId,
        "outputs",
        "results",
        "result"));

Runtime

Parameter object is used for

RuntimeParamsUpdate

Set shared/run parameters

RuntimeRunParams

submits normal frames or EPICRAW3 and runs the graph

RuntimePassiveBinoFrame Submit EPICRAW3 raw data in

passive_bino mode

RuntimePassiveBinoImage

describes a single original image when constructing EPICRAW3

BindingRef

Read binding output value or raw point cloud

PointCloudRef

Read and parse bound point clouds

RuntimeBindingDataUpdate

Set graph binding input data

RuntimeStrategyParamsUpdate

Set policy parameters

FileParamRef

Query file parameters MD5

SingleNodeParams

runs a single node directly without building a graph. It is recommended to cooperate with RunSingleNodeNoGraphParsedAsync to automatically parse the output.

RuntimeStrategyParamsUpdate currently only works with PoseListFilter, PickPointFilter, PoseListSorterInXOY、PickPointSorterInXOY、PickPointSorterNew、 PoseListSorter These 6 types of nodes. Its ParamsData generally starts from Runtime.GetNodeParamsInfoWithStrategyAsync(…​) Take out paramsData in the return value, modify the fields that need to be updated and then return them as a whole.

await client.Runtime.SetRunParamsAsync(
    new RuntimeParamsUpdate("demo_graph", new { threshold = 0.7 }));

var result = await client.Runtime.GetBindedOutputValueAsync(
    new BindingRef("demo_graph", "result"));

RuntimeRunParams has two input modes:

mode Construction method What should be passed?

Normal mode

new RuntimeRunParams(graphName, frames)

One or more RuntimeFrame

Passive binocular mode

RuntimeRunParams.PassiveBinoFromFile/Bytes/Images(…​)

a RuntimePassiveBinoFrame

Do not mix the two modes. The normal mode transmits the complete EPICRAW; the passive binocular mode transmits the dedicated passive binocular EPICRAW3. In normal mode, RuntimeFrame is constructed first and then RuntimeRunParams is put in:

var frame = RuntimeFrame.FromBytes(epicRawBytes, cam2Base);

var runResult = await client.Runtime.RunGraphResultAsync(
    new RuntimeRunParams("demo_graph", new[] { frame }));
Console.WriteLine($"Run request status: {runResult.Status}");

You can also use RuntimeFrame.FromFile(…​) to read the file, or RuntimeFrame.FromData(…​) to generate EPICRAW2/3 locally from RuntimePointData, RuntimeImageData and camera parameters. It is recommended to use the RuntimeRunParams factory method in passive binocular mode to avoid forgetting RunMode:

var runResult = await client.Runtime.RunGraphAsync(
    RuntimeRunParams.PassiveBinoFromFile(
        "demo_graph",
        "/data/passive_bino.epicraw",
        cam2Base));

Use RuntimeRunParams.PassiveBinoFromBytes(…​) when there is already EPICRAW3 bytes. Use RuntimeRunParams.PassiveBinoFromImages(…​) when there are three original images, the image object is new RuntimePassiveBinoImage(data, width, height, matType), matType uses OpenCV Mat type encoding. passiveBinoParams of PassiveBinoFromImages(…​) needs to contain DepthSrc1, DepthSrc2, TextureSrc and metadata, each of which must contain the following four fields:

var cameraParams = new Dictionary<string, object?>
{
    ["CameraMatrix"] = new[]
    {
        2113.997971632298, 0, 1956.222038925553,
        0, 2113.7299751270057, 1505.0473199581195,
        0, 0, 1,
    },
    ["CameraDistortion"] = new[]
    {
        0.049901632334, -0.037810281265, -0.00048319461,
        -0.000276258172, -0.026886293015,
    },
    ["CameraRotation"] = new[]
    {
        0.9995132330503337, -0.005059159488191983, -0.030784766728731865,
        0.004951704878090689, 0.9999813828533568, -0.003565748937897527,
        0.030802233296787017, 0.003411576169582241, 0.999519676430619,
    },
    ["CameraTranslation"] = new[]
    {
        -25.837377992238334, -0.6852264771262435, -4.372034519324568,
    },
};

var passiveBinoParams = new Dictionary<string, object?>
{
    ["DepthSrc1"] = cameraParams,
    ["DepthSrc2"] = cameraParams,
    ["TextureSrc"] = cameraParams,
};

Use the binding name when setting up graph binding input data:

await client.Runtime.SetGraphBindingDataAsync(
    new RuntimeBindingDataUpdate(
        "demo_graph",
        new Dictionary<string, object?>
        {
            ["image_input"] = imageBytes,
            ["threshold"] = 0.7,
        }));

Easy to make mistakes

1. The connection sequence is output to input

The constructor order of both NodeConnectionParams and SubGraphConnectionParams is:

graphName, outputNodeId, outputPortName, inputNodeId, inputPortName

That is, first write the node and port from which data flows out, and then write the node and port from which data flows in. It is recommended to use named parameters to reduce typos.

2. Use RuntimeService for single-node direct operation.

Runtime Single node direct operation can receive inputs such as byte[], FileInfo, SingleNodeFileInput, strings, numbers, etc. When encountering FileInfo / byte[] / local path string, SDK will automatically handle it according to the node input port type: * File Input only transmits the path string and does not read the file content. * ColorImage / Image paths will be converted into base64 image lists. * The .ply paths of point cloud ports such as XYZPoints / NormalPoints will be converted to Atom point cloud binary. * When the port type cannot be queried, byte[] or file content will still be uploaded as file fields according to the old rules.

var result = await client.Runtime.RunSingleNodeNoGraphParsedAsync(
    new SingleNodeParams(
        "ImageNode",
        inputs: new Dictionary<string, object?>
        {
            ["image"] = new FileInfo("/data/test.png"),
        }));

If you use the recommended RunSingleNodeNoGraphParsedAsync, SingleNodeParams can also fill in OutputDataTypes / OutputPointDims: * OutputDataTypes tells SDK which outputs are of XYZPoints, ColorImage, etc. parsable types. * OutputPointDims is used for point cloud output dimension prompts; XYZPoints defaults to 3, NormalPoints/RGBPoints defaults to 6. * When not filled in, SDK will press NodeName to query the node output port type; if the server returns raw bytes, it needs to be able to determine the only point cloud output port.

3. RuntimeFrame field name is different from the server field name

The field name in C# is Cam2Base. SDK will be converted into cam2Base required by the server when packaging the request. Cam2Base The server currently only supports the rotation vector form: [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] with length 6 (translation + Rodrigues rotation vector), and does not support 4x4/3x4 matrices; SDK will verify the length when constructing RuntimeFrame/RuntimePassiveBinoFrame, and will throw ArgumentException if it is not satisfied.

4. The simple interface still transfers strings directly

The following interfaces still retain direct string parameters:

await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync("my_graph");
await client.Graph.RunGraphResultAsync("my_graph");
await client.Runtime.LoadGraphAsync("my_graph");
await client.Runtime.GetMetaInfoModelAsync("my_graph");

If an interface requires multiple business fields, use parameter objects.
